rendered: The authors did not use a carbonate electrolyte with the sodium metal anode. As opposed to traditional organic carbonate electrolytes, the coin cells were assembled with NaPF6 salt dissolved in tetraglyme, a glyme-based electrolyte.[1][2] The reason given is that carbonate-based electrolytes form an unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on Na metal anodes. The glyme electrolyte was chosen to overcome this problem, building on earlier studies that showed sodium anode stability during reversible plating in glymes. The authors state that a stable SEI is critical to achieving good cycling performance.[3][4][5][6]
